copy.title: The Ronaldo Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Cristiano Ronaldo’s family: Al-Nassr, Nike, the CR7 hotels, Perplexity, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #025 · The Ronaldo family · Data as of
copy.h1: Football’s first billionaire has a family. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them runs, which companies you can buy stock in, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they run, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. Cristiano’s five children appear by first name only.
copy.investLede: His own businesses are private. Nike, which pays him under a lifetime deal, trades on the NYSE, but the family doesn’t own it.
copy.moneyLede: Mostly pay. Forbes says he’s the first active athlete to earn more than $2 billion before taxes and fees, and that Al-Nassr pays him more than $200 million a year. He’s the only one here with a published net worth.
copy.recordLede: What his contracts, deals and a Spanish court record show. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From Funchal, Madeira, to football’s first billionaire.

summary.t: A municipal gardener and part-time kit man at the local club, Andorinha. He died in 2005 at 52.
Worked as a cook and cleaner when Cristiano was young. Since her husband died in 2005 she has been the head of the family.
Cristiano’s oldest sibling. A businesswoman with a jewelry line and a clothing store dedicated to her brother.
Cristiano’s older brother. He runs the museum dedicated to Cristiano in Madeira.

The Portuguese star played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus before joining Saudi club Al-Nassr in 2023. In October 2025 Bloomberg called him the first footballer to become a billionaire.

owns.t: Plays for the club and holds a reported 15% stake under his 2025 contract.
Owns the hotel brand 50-50 with the Pestana Hotel Group.
Investor since December 2025; stake not disclosed.

record.t: His new contract, signed in June 2025, was reportedly worth more than $400 million: an annual salary of £177 million ($237.5 million), plus bonuses and a reported 15% stake in the club.

Nike has sponsored him since 2003 and signed him to a lifetime deal in November 2016, making him its third lifetime athlete after Michael Jordan and LeBron James. Terms weren’t disclosed; Bloomberg estimates the deal pays him nearly $18 million a year.
He and the Pestana Hotel Group split the €75 million first phase 50-50, about €37 million each. Pestana CR7 hotels now operate in Funchal, Lisbon, Madrid, Marrakech and New York.
In January 2019 he accepted a 23-month suspended sentence and an €18.8 million fine in a Madrid court, in a case over his image-rights income in Spain from 2011 to 2014.

facts.t: Forbes ranked him the world’s highest-paid athlete in 2026, the fourth year in a row.
He has nearly 1 billion followers across Instagram, Facebook and X, Forbes says.
Hopper HQ estimated in 2024 that he could charge about $3.4 million for one sponsored Instagram post.
He had 973 career goals at the start of the 2026 World Cup and wants to be the first to reach 1,000.

kidsNote.t: Cristiano has five children: Cristiano Jr., the twins Eva and Mateo, and his daughters with Georgina, Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda. We list first names only.

summary.t: Cristiano’s older sister, a singer with records such as Pronta P’ra Te Amar.

Born in Buenos Aires and raised in Spain, she met Cristiano in 2016 while working at a Gucci store in Madrid. She produces and stars in the Netflix series I Am Georgina and started the clothing brand OM by G in 2021.

record.t: They married in a civil ceremony at home in Cascais on Aug. 11, 2026, a year to the day after announcing their engagement. They married under a separation-of-assets regime, Euronews reported.

facts.t: She launched an activewear line, Mimoa, in 2026.
